system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall:** The Seller's "fair and balanced package" is in fact a one-sided seller draft on nearly every point. Several positions (Fundamental/Title folded into general caps; limitations applying to *all* Claims including fraud; whole-data-room disclosure; blanket buyer-knowledge bar) collapse the protections our playbook treats as non-negotiable. No fallback authority from Amelia Frost has been given on cap or claims period, so we hold starting positions. Note also the Disclosure Letter candidly confirms that Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout and Ironquay assignment are all **not** in the data room – useful admissions for our mark-up.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, which has not been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl. 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first dollar once exceeded).
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl. 12.3/13), plus a default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the default rule would silently sweep Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnity claims into the general regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside de minimis, basket and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright – non-negotiable.** Paying AUD 24m for shares with title recourse capped at AUD 4.8m and 18 months is commercially unacceptable; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) – no fraud carve-out.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express carve-out.** This is a no-waiver item for us and a provision purporting to cap liability for the Seller's own fraud is likely unenforceable anyway – its inclusion signals the draft's overall direction.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]-[1.2]); plus a no-admission reservation at [1.4].
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; delete whole-data-room / public-register / prudent-search deeming.
- Recommendation: **Reject [1.1]-[1.2] and Sch 7 general disclosure; accept only the specific items in sections 2–10 as disclosed, each tested for fairness.** Whole-data-room disclosure would neutralise most of the warranty package by deeming every document (and every public filing) known to us.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; if any qualifier survives, limit to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, with seller warranties qualified by named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl. 8.3.** "Discoverable" knowledge imputed to advisers is a constructive-knowledge bar that, combined with SPA-N-006, would leave almost nothing to claim on.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl. 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional written consent under cl. 11.2 **and** (b) evidence that all cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" with specific steps.
- Recommendation: **Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours; redraft CP.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – a conditional consent whose conditions later fail is no consent at all.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2/7). DL §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter before Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds (debt-free/cash-free); executed security releases/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release only on irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** Without this we acquire a company still encumbered by AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a change-of-control default risk under cl. 8.1.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals as applicable) either as a specific deduction line item in funds flow or expressly seller-funded with a specific indemnity.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require line item or specific indemnity, and request on-cost quantification.** Bonuses triggered by Completion are a transaction cost the Seller has effectively asked the Company (i.e., us) to absorb post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl. 11.1). DL §4: DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering loss of or defective title to the Project Materials, third-party claims and costs of obtaining confirmatory assignment; preserve the cure path (seller pays SOW3 balance pre-Completion and procures confirmatory assignment); treat AUD 180,000 as unverified – obtain bank/Ironquay confirmation.
- Recommendation: **Reject "adequate"; broaden indemnity and add pre-Completion cure deliverable.** The real exposure is IP ownership, not the payment amount, and the amount itself is unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl. 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: link sent to unintended external address, ~1,240 records, access/scope/notification duty undetermined; no breach characterised, no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: covenant to preserve logs and evidence, complete and document the investigation, provide updates and conclusions pre-Completion, cooperate on any regulator/notification analysis; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident; no assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric exposure either way.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "not material" conclusion as premature; add investigation/update covenant and specific indemnity.** Materiality cannot be assessed until access and notification questions are resolved, and the Seller's own letter concedes they are not.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8: three related AUD 110,000 renewals (DD-008/DD-011), silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: information – timing, termination rights, whether accrued/committed pre-Completion, business necessity – before classifying; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction, but equally no acceptance of "ordinary course" on assertion.
- Recommendation: **Assess, don't concede or deduct yet; issue a DD request and reserve position.** The Seller's own disclosure declines to state the facts that would support its ordinary-course characterisation.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: general limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl. 12.3/13); limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; Title and Tax/IP folded into general regime.
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, debt adjustments) and covenants/specific indemnities; general caps/baskets/time limits apply only to general Warranty Claims; no catch-all override.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft cl. 12/13 so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and expressly exclude the other categories.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a hidden general-regime override that undoes every carve-out we negotiate.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and not that Buyer has verified it.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical filings, share certificates, board minutes/transfer history, PPSR and encumbrance searches, Riverlark security scope, constitutional/pre-emptive right compliance, seller capacity and authority documents; full Fundamental warranty and 100% cap per SPA-N-004.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient; complete independent verification before signing.** The register is a seller-controlled internal record and the Seller itself declines to say more than that it is the "source relied on".

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (i.e., 20% cap, 18 months, AUD 25k/250k thresholds).
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN as separate regimes – tax typically covered by a tax indemnity with a longer period (aligned to statutory review periods), IP warranties with their own period/cap; neither folded into general limits. Per playbook, assume no unlimited liability and no resolution yet.
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our record shows agreement, and the Seller's characterisation is an attempt to close by assertion what has never been negotiated.

---

**Suggested priority order for the mark-up / next call:**
1. Category separation + Fundamental/Title + fraud carve-out (SPA-N-004/005/014) – structural, must be fixed before numbers matter.
2. Disclosure scope + buyer knowledge (SPA-N-006/007) – otherwise warranty package is illusory.
3. Bluefen CP and Riverlark completion mechanics (SPA-N-008/009) – gating completion risk.
4. Cap/thresholds/time (SPA-N-001/002/003) – hold starting positions; flag to Amelia Frost that Seller is at our fallback levels but no authority exists.
5. Specific money items (SPA-N-010/011/013) and incident covenant (SPA-N-012).
6. Title verification and Tax/IP (SPA-N-015/016) – DD workstream and open list.

Let me know if you'd like this converted into a rider-style mark-up table or an issues list for Amelia Frost.
=== END ADVICE ===
